# Two migration stories in one line

[New Zealand's net migration hit a record 135,529 in the year to October 2023. The headline number hid two opposite movements underneath it.]{.standfirst}

*Prototype A of 3 — Quarto + Closeread. Scroll to advance.*

:::

::: {.cr-section}

## Net migration, 2001 to today {focus-on="cr-total"}

Each point is the net gain of migrants over the previous 12 months. The line spent two decades between 10,000 and 70,000.

## Then came the post-border surge {focus-on="cr-peak"}

Net migration peaked at 135,529 in the year to October 2023, far above anything in the previous two decades.

## One line, two very different stories {focus-on="cr-split"}

Splitting by citizenship shows the total hides an offset. Non-New Zealand citizens drove the surge while New Zealand citizens left in growing numbers.

## New Zealanders left at a record rate {focus-on="cr-trough"}

Net migration of New Zealand citizens bottomed at -45,915 in the year to April 2024.

## Where it sits now {focus-on="cr-latest"}

The total has fallen back to 24,250 in the year to March 2026.

## What this prototype shows

Closeread swaps between five pre-rendered Plotly figures. It does not animate
between them, so the transition is a cross-fade rather than a line redraw.
Getting a true redraw would mean writing the Plotly transition calls by hand,
at which point the extension is doing less of the work.

<p class="data-source">Source: Statistics NZ ITM552301 — migrant arrivals and departures by citizenship. 12-month rolling sum.</p>

:::
